paragraphs: Friend, this passage teaches us that the Bible lets a hurting man say it all out loud. Job remembers the days when God's lamp shone above his head, and then he says the light he looked for turned to darkness. He doesn't clean it up or pretend. He says he cried out to God and felt like God didn't answer (Job 29:3; 30:20, 26).

Here's what that means for you. You don't have to put on a nice face before you come to God. Job pours out his whole aching heart, and Scripture keeps every word of it for us to read. Honest pain is not the opposite of faith, and I figure God can handle a whole speech of it.

Now look at what Job holds onto even in the mess. He remembers that the good he did was real: he rescued the poor who cried out and wept for those in trouble (Job 29:12; 30:25). Hold onto the good you've done, friend, but don't make it your whole footing. This story is FAR from finished, and the God Job is talking to is still there, listening.
